title: Hardcoding audit
description: Every distinct `entity_ref` the extraction found, with its source repo, its inferred scope and its repo's naming-convention label. This is the second committed facts store, and it carries identifiers from all four repos including the two that grant nothing: an entry holds a `domain.object_id`, a scope and a naming-convention label, and none of those is authored text, which is what a licence withholds. The entry field set is closed, so a field that could hold an alias, a display name, a comment or a YAML fragment cannot be added without editing this file and the allowlist together. The two patterns below are the ones `schemas/catalog/fact-shapes.yaml` declares for `entity_ref` and `slug`; task 3.6 routes this entry schema through `fact-fields.yaml` and `fact-shapes.yaml` exactly as task 3.5 does for `raw-behaviors.json`, and until then a test asserts the inlined patterns equal the declared shapes so the two cannot drift apart in the meantime.

constant.description: The fixed things a reference may target instead of a slot. Deliberately heterogeneous -- `device_id` is a targeting key while the others are entity domains -- because the property the justification needs is a single one, and each entry records which kind it is.

entity_ref.description: The literal as the source spells it. A fact about someone's naming scheme, and the only place a raw identifier of this kind is committed outside `raw-behaviors.json`.

repo.description: The repo the reference was found in. Resolved against `catalog/repos.yaml` by the validator, which can join the two files; a JSON Schema reference cannot reach into a YAML document's contents.

scope.description: Inferred from where the reference sits, so the same concept can be compared across repos.

naming_convention.description: The repo's naming-convention label, as a slug. A slug rather than an enum because the label set is fixed when task 3.6 sees the data; what is fixed now, and what matters for the licence position, is that the field cannot hold a sentence.

slot.description: The slot this reference maps to, or null when it maps to a constant. A reference to the runtime `slot` schema's own name property rather than a copy of its pattern: a restated pattern is a second definition of a slot name, free to drift from the published one, and it is the thing the conformance check in task 7.6 exists to catch. Resolved against `catalog/slots.yaml` in task 5.3.

constant.description: The justification, when the reference is one of the fixed things rather than a slot.

allOf.description: A reference that resolves to neither a slot nor a constant fails the build, so every entry either feeds the slot vocabulary or says why it cannot.
